claims.text: Automatic Voter Registration (AVR) increases voter registration by 1.8 percentage points among the full electorate.
Automatic Voter Registration (AVR) increases voter registration by 3.5 percentage points among young voters.
Automatic Voter Registration (AVR) does not impact individual-level turnout.
Implementation of an AVR policy is not associated with an increase in voter registration for individuals who moved within the past year.
Implementation of an AVR policy is not associated with an increase in turnout for individuals who moved within the past year.

evidence.description: Difference in difference estimates suggest that AVR increases registration by 1.8 percentage points among the full electorate.
Difference in difference estimates indicate AVR increases registration by 3.5 percentage points among young voters.
Difference in difference estimates show AVR does not impact individual-level turnout.
The implementation of an AVR policy is not associated with an increase in registration for those who have moved within the past year.
The implementation of an AVR policy is not associated with an increase in turnout for those who have moved within the past year.

methodologies.name: Difference-in-differences estimation
methodologies.description: Evaluated the impact of statewide opt-out AVR policy adoption on registration and turnout across the electorate and subgroups using survey data from 2012 to 2024.
conditions: Adoption of opt-out Automatic Voter Registration (AVR)
